conventions: Predicate participles of the hymnic chain describing God are read by whether an article stands on them: anarthrous ones (v2 עֹטֶה, נוֹטֶה; v4 עֹשֶׂה; v13 מַשְׁקֶה; v14 מַצְמִיחַ) keep the ASV's supplied Who or He in the participle's own unit, headed on the lexical verb, on the reasoning of rules 41/46; arthrous ones (v3, v10, v32) give the Who/He to the article under rule 41; the finite יָסַד of v5 leaves its Who added under rule 55. The competing reading marks the anarthrous Who/He added and is named in each verse note.

The archaic connective vowel-suffix וֹ on construct חַיְתוֹ (v11 חַיְתוֹ שָׂדָי, v20 חַיְתוֹ־יָעַר), which MACULA segments as Sp3ms, is not a possessive and the ASV writes nothing for it; it is its own unrepresented unit beside the construct noun, which keeps beast/beasts and the rectum its of-phrase.

A possessive the ASV supplies on an object noun where no suffix stands is added (v12 'have their habitation', v15 'his face', v17 'make their nests'), the light-verb complement keeping only its own noun; where an assimilated article stands on the noun the article takes the possessive under rule 41 (v21 לַטָּרֶף → 'after their prey').
report: Read all 35 verses end to end against the 45-lemma candidate table and the added units the table cannot see. No construction is analysed two ways without a source difference licensing it.

Supplied relative/subject on participles is consistent: anarthrous participles (v2, v4, v13, v14) keep Who/He in the participle's unit; arthrous ones (v3, v10, v32) give it to the article under rule 41; the finite verb of v5 leaves Who added under rule 55. Each verse note records the competing reading.

Supplied possessives are consistent: added where no suffix or article stands (v12 their, v15 his, v17 their); the assimilated article of v21 takes their under rule 41. Supplied subordinators (v5, v9, v15) are added wherever no morpheme stands and go to the לְ where one does (v14, v27). Elliptical 'with X as with Y' (v2, v6) gives both withs to the verb under rule 25 in both verses.
Suffix, article, preposition and waw variation in the table is all ASV-driven (rectum of vs bare, every vs all, as vs like, for/after/on/are for) and licensed by rules 14, 15, 19, 40, 41, 49, 52.

BSB disagreements are all convention differences, none a genuine error: recasting silences עַל (v5), מִ (v15), בֶּ (v32) and the infinitive's לְ (v21) under rules 40/52; the unrendered second member of עוֹלָם וָעֶד and its waw (v5), the waw before אֵין מִסְפָּר (v25), the archaic connective suffix on חַיְתוֹ (v11, v20), the resumptive suffix on אֵינָם (v35) and the 15 paragogic nuns are unrepresented under rules 14, 22, 32 and 50.

Reviewed and left standing: v20 'creep forth' keeps forth with the verb (rule 44 lists forth among the particles it keeps); v26 'There is leviathan' takes the presentative frame on the noun rather than distributing שָׁם, with the alternative noted; v27 'due' on the suffix of עִתּוֹ with the alternative noted. None is a chapter split.
Nothing here generalises beyond what the contract already states; no promotion or amendment.
